You will strengthen coordination with other business units and external stakeholders, oversee annual business and procurement plans, and ensure supply chain input is included in project design and strategic planning. You will monitor action plans for identified challenges, submit procurement plans on time, and maintain accurate asset registers and disposal records. Role Purpose The Field Engineer will provide Field-level Technical support, Supervision and quality control for Save the Children International's construction, rehabilitation and retrofitting projects in the assigned duty station. The post holder will support technical assessments, design and BoQ review, procurement, construction and retrofitting supervision, quality assurance, measurement, contractor monitoring and completion/handover. The Field Engineer will ensure that works comply with approved drawings, BoQs, specifications, contracts, SCI standards, applicable regulations, donor requirements, health and safety and safeguarding standards. Particular emphasis will be placed on the assessment and retrofitting of existing buildings , ensuring that interventions are compatible with existing structural conditions, technically sound, climate-resilient, safe, accessible and cost-effective. Scope Of Role Reports to: Construction Engineer/Manager Staff reporting to this post :N/A Budget Responsibilities: N/A Role Dimensions Internal: Construction Engineer/Manager, Area/Field Manager, Programme, Supply Chain, Finance, WASH, Education and Operations teams External: Contractors, consultants, suppliers, local authorities, government technical departments, school management committees, communities and other stakeholders Key Accountabilites Technical Assessment, Design and Planning Conduct technical assessments of existing and proposed infrastructure, including buildings, foundations, roofs, walls, floors, drainage and WASH facilities. Identify structural defects, deterioration, safety risks and retrofitting/rehabilitation requirements. Take accurate site measurements and collect relevant technical information. Prepare assessment reports with findings, photographs, recommendations and estimated intervention requirements. Prepare, review or validate technical drawings, BoQs, cost estimates and specifications. Verify quantities against drawings, specifications and actual site conditions. Review retrofitting solutions for compatibility with existing structures and identify design gaps or technical risks. Provide technical feedback on consultant designs and contractor submissions. Incorporate climate resilience, accessibility, inclusion, safety, durability and maintainability into technical solutions. Escalate significant structural or design issues to the Construction Engineer/Manager. Construction, Rehabilitation and Retrofitting Supervision Support site handover and contractor mobilization. Conduct regular supervision of construction, rehabilitation and retrofitting works. Verify setting-out, dimensions, levels, materials, methods and workmanship. Closely monitor retrofitting works to ensure structural integrity and compatibility with existing buildings. Inspect foundations, structural elements, masonry, roofing, drainage, WASH facilities and finishes. Monitor compliance with approved drawings, BoQs, specifications and contract requirements. Monitor work progress against approved programmes. Identify defects, delays and deviations and follow up corrective action. Participate in site and progress meetings. Escalate significant technical, contractual, safety or implementation issues to the Construction Engineer/Manager. Quality Assurance, Measurement and Contract Support Inspect materials and workmanship and monitor compliance with approved standards. Conduct or witness required inspections and tests. Identify and document defects and non-conformities and follow up corrective actions. Maintain inspection, testing and photographic records. Measure completed works against approved BoQs. Verify quantities and contractor progress/payment claims. Identify incomplete, defective or non-compliant work before payment recommendation. Review proposed variations and additional works and provide technical justification. Submit technical recommendations on payments and variations to the Construction Engineer/Manager. Support final inspection, completion and handover. Climate Resilience, HSE, Safeguarding and Reporting Ensure construction and retrofitting works address relevant climate risks, particularly flooding, drainage and erosion. Promote durable, maintainable and cost-effective construction solutions. Ensure accessibility for children and people with disabilities. Monitor health and safety requirements, including PPE and risks associated with excavation, working at height, lifting, electrical and structural works. Minimize risks to children, staff, workers and surrounding communities. Ensure safeguarding requirements are observed at school and community sites. Monitor environmental impacts and waste management. Prepare technical progress updates and maintain assessment, supervision, measurement and inspection records. Maintain photographic documentation and trackers for progress, defects and corrective actions. Provide technical inputs to Programme and donor reports and completion documentation. Report serious safety, safeguarding, environmental or technical risks promptly. Review, Follow up and Assessment The Field Engineer will be responsible for regular review, follow-up and assessment of assigned construction and retrofitting activities, including: Reviewing technical designs, drawings, BoQs and specifications. Following up construction, rehabilitation and retrofitting works against approved requirements. Monitoring contractor performance, quality, progress and compliance. Verifying completed works and contractor payment requests. Assessing technical risks, implementation challenges and required corrective actions. Following up defects and non-conformities until satisfactory resolution. Participating in planning, procurement, construction and post-construction activities. Providing technical advice to communities, school management structures and other stakeholders. Supporting practical capacity building on construction monitoring and maintenance. Providing timely technical feedback and recommendations to the Construction Engineer/Manager. The post holder may also support SCI emergency response and other infrastructure activities as required. Creativity Develops and encourages new and innovative solutions Willing to take disciplined risks. Integrity Honest encourages opennessand transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity. Minimum 3 years of relevant professional experience in construction, rehabilitation, renovation or retrofitting for diploma holders and at least two years of relevant professional experience for degree holders. Experience And Skills Demonstrated experience in construction site supervision and contractor management. Experience in preparation and review of drawings, BoQs, cost estimates and technical specifications. Experience in measurement, quantity verification and payment assessment. Good knowledge of construction materials, methods and quality control. Knowledge of occupational health and safety requirements. Good technical report writing and documentation skills. Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel. Ability and willingness to travel and work in challenging field environments Experience in rehabilitation and retrofitting existing buildings. Experience with school or community infrastructure. Experience in WASH infrastructure, drainage and flood mitigation. Experience in climate-resilient construction. Previous experience with NGO, humanitarian or development programmes. Knowledge of applicable South Sudan construction standards and regulations. Knowledge of AutoCAD, Revit or other relevant engineering software. Knowledge of Arabic and/or relevant local languages. review_candidates.description: Rejoignez le CNP Saint-Martin et devenez notre prochain.e collègue (H/F/X) Vous êtes éducateur et accompagner des usagers résidant dans des Maisons de Soins Psychiatrique vous motive? Le Centre Neuro Psychiatrique Saint-Martin est un acteur de premier plan dans le domaine de la santé mentale et des réseaux de soins, au cœur de la Wallonie. Nous nous engageons à offrir un soutien essentiel à celles et ceux qui en ont le plus besoin. Aujourd'hui, nous recherchons un éducateur (H/F/X) transversal pour accompagner les usagers résidants dans ses Maisons de soins psychiatriques (MSP) mixtes « Sénevé », « Mériba » et « Les Entours ». PRESENTATION DE L'UNITE Les MSP Sont Des Lieux D’accueil Mixtes, De Résidence Et De Soins Inscrits Dans Le Cadre De La Fonction 5 De La Réforme Des Soins En Santé Mentale. Situées Dans Un Cadre Confortable, Moderne Et Proche Aussi Bien De La Ville Que La Nature, Nos Trois MSP Sont Des Habitats Spécifiques Destinés à Accueillir Des Résident(e)s Adultes Nécessitant Un Accompagnement Continu Soit Provisoire, Soit à Plus Long Terme. Cet Accompagnement Se Réalise Dans Les Tâches Quotidiennes De La Vie Communautaire Mais Aussi à Travers Un Panel D’activités. Chaque Accompagnement S’adapte à l’histoire de vie de chaque résident, à ses besoins et à sa pathologie. Vise l’autonomisation et la réalisation de soi. Se définit à partir d’un projet de vie, de soins individualisés. Se réalise à travers une approche pluridisciplinaire (infirmier, psychologue, éducateur, assistant social, psychiatre, …). S’articule avec le réseau social et familial du résident. Les MSP « Mériba » et « Les Entours » accueillent des résidents souffrant d’un trouble psychiatrique stabilisé de type psychose ou schizophrénie. La MSP « Sénevé » accueille des patients porteurs d’un double diagnostique (handicap mental léger à modéré et maladie mentale). sur le plan psychopédagogique et dans un projet de réhabilitation psychosociale soit en résidentiel ou en ambulatoire. VOTRE MISSION L’éducateur , en partenariat avec le bénéficiaire , les proches et l’ensemble des intervenants internes et externes impliqués dans la prise en charge, réalise au quotidien des activités/ateliers/accompagnements Il met en œuvre des méthodes et des techniques spécifiques pédagogiques , sociales et psychologiques appropriées visant le développement personnel, la maturation sociale et l'autonomie du/des bénéficiaires et des proches. Ses interventions sont orientées « care » et « cure » et s’inscrivent pleinement dans la réforme de soins de santé mentale pour jeunes, adolescents, adultes et personnes âgées. NOUS VOUS OFFRONS Un contrat à durée indéterminée à temps plein de jour (40h00 par semaine). Une rémunération conforme au barème IFIC et aux conventions collectives de travail en vigueur. Un jour de repos compensatoire par mois. Des chèques-repas ainsi qu’une intervention dans les frais de déplacement. Un large choix de formations et un accompagnement individualisé, pour que vous puissiez continuer à évoluer dans un domaine qui vous passionne. Un environnement de travail verdoyant Une atmosphère de travail positive où le bien-être n’est pas juste un concept, mais une réalité quotidienne. Et de nombreux avantages repris dans la brochure ci-jointe : https://cp-st-martin.be/uploads/pdf/brochure_avantages_CNP_St-Martin_20240304.pdf VOTRE PROFIL Être titulaire d’un diplôme d’éducateur spécialisé en accompagnement psycho-éducatif. Avoir des compétences en relation d’aide, observation, analyse, planification et évaluation. Avoir la capacité à travailler en équipe. Faire preuve de créativité. Aimer travailler avec les animaux est un atout. Posséder des connaissances en santé mentale constitue un plus. Disposer d’une expérience dans une fonction similaire et la possession du visa d’aide-soignant sont des atouts supplémentaires. VOTRE CANDIDATURE Au CNP Saint-Martin, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité est une richesse. Nous accueillons toutes les candidatures et garantissons un processus de recrutement fondé sur les compétences, l’expérience et les motivations, sans distinction de genre, d’âge, d’origine, de nationalité, de convictions religieuses, d’orientation sexuelle ou de situation de handicap. Pour postuler, merci de déposer votre CV et votre lettre de motivation, en cliquant sur le lien Postuler.

review_candidates.title: E T Consultant, Blended Finance Investment Officer - req39622
review_candidates.description: E T Consultant, Blended Finance Investment Officer Job #: req39622 Organization: IFC Sector: Investment Grade: EC3 Term Duration: 2 years 0 months Recruitment Type: Local Recruitment Location: Brussels,Belgium Required Language(s): English Preferred Language(s): French Closing Date: 12/10/2026 (MM/DD/YYYY) at 11:59pm UTC Description At the International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group (WBG), you’ll join a diverse, global community working across cultures, disciplines, and borders to address the world’s most pressing development challenges. With 1.2 billion young people reaching working age in the decade ahead, the challenge of job creation has never been greater. Through partnerships across 145 countries and more than 182 offices worldwide, we work with governments, private sector, development partners and other stakeholders to invest in people, strengthen markets, and deliver scalable, data-driven solutions that generate more and better jobs and improve lives. In fiscal year 2026, IFC committed a record $105.6 billion to private companies and financial institutions in developing countries. For more information, visit www.ifc.org . Blended Finance is an important tool for enabling IFC investments in markets and sectors where risks or other market barriers prevent projects with strong development impact from proceeding on fully commercial terms. CBFNP manages and deploys concessional resources from a range of partners alongside IFC's own-account investments, with the objective of addressing clearly identified market failures while minimizing concessionality and avoiding market distortion. IFC has a growing portfolio of partnerships with the European Commission, including guarantees under the European Fund for Sustainable Development Plus (EFSD+). IFC's Better Futures Program for the real sector is supported through EFSD+ guarantees and is intended to facilitate private-sector investment across eligible emerging markets. IFC currently needs to accelerate conversion of the EFSD+ pipeline into committed transactions, which is important both for deployment of existing guarantee capacity and IFC's positioning for future EC guarantee programs. CBFNP therefore seeks a Brussels-based Extended Term Consultant, Blended Finance Investment Officer with a primary focus on real-sector transactions. The position will combine hands-on BF transaction work with pipeline origination, engagement with IFC industry and regional teams, coordination around European concessional facilities, and systematic market intelligence on how European DFIs and other development institutions deploy concessional donor resources. The Brussels location is intended to place this investment expertise closer to European Commission counterparts and the broader European development-finance ecosystem while retaining a strong transaction and commercial orientation. Duties And Accountabilities Origination and development of the EFSD+ pipeline Proactively identify INR and MAS projects where EFSD+ guarantees or other blended-finance instruments could address a clearly identified market failure and enable an otherwise constrained IFC investment. Work upstream with IFC regional and industry investment teams to identify BF opportunities before financing structures become fixed, rather than introducing BF late in transaction processing. Translate EFSD+ eligibility, geographic allocations and donor priorities into practical pipeline opportunities for IFC Investment teams. Help maintain a forward-looking EFSD+ pipeline, identifying constraints that could prevent projects from reaching BFC endorsement, Board approval, commitment and EFSD+ inclusion. Support prioritization of transactions based on development impact, additionality, likelihood of execution and efficient use of scarce concessional resources. Blended-finance structuring and transaction execution Structure and process BF co-investments alongside IFC own-account investments, with particular emphasis on guarantees/first-loss structures, including for structured debt and equity/quasi-equity, providing local-currency solutions, and other innovative risk-sharing structures. Translate donor risk appetite and facility requirements into structures that address the project's underlying market constraint while limiting concessionality. Assess the BF counterfactual, market failure, additionality, pricing/subsidy, minimum concessionality and potential market distortion. Work closely with transaction teams throughout the investment cycle, including early-look discussions, appraisal, BFC endorsement and approval, IRM/Board processing, commitment and post-commitment execution. Maintain accountability to the Blended Finance Committee through clear and balanced presentation of the commercial, financial and development rationale to be considered for Blended Finance. EFSD+ coordination and European Commission engagement Serve as a BF Investment Officer focal point for EFSD+ pipeline development, working closely with the CBFNP facility team. Support engagement with relevant European Commission counterparts in Brussels on pipeline, transaction eligibility and implementation issues. Help translate evolving EC priorities and requirements into clear, actionable guidance for IFC investment teams. Feed transaction experience back into facility implementation and future program design so that donor requirements remain workable for private-sector transactions. Support BF Facility and Partnerships colleagues in European donor discussions where transaction, structuring or market knowledge is needed. Market intelligence on use of concessional finance by European DFIs A specific responsibility of the Brussels position will be to build systematic market intelligence on the use of donor-funded concessional finance by other European development institutions. The IO Will Track relevant transactions and structures used by institutions such as the EBRD, EIB and European bilateral DFIs, particularly where EU/EC or other donor resources are blended with own-account financing. Compare financing structures, guarantee coverage, pricing, tenor, risk-sharing arrangements and, to the extent information is available, levels of concessionality. Identify emerging approaches and instruments that may affect IFC's competitiveness or provide lessons for future IFC BF structures. Maintain a practical transaction-comparables database for use by BF IOs and investment teams. Incorporate relevant market intelligence into BFC notes, pipeline discussions and facility negotiations where appropriate. Identify potential opportunities for parallel financing, mobilization or collaboration with European DFIs. Portfolio and post-commitment support Support supervision of assigned BF investments, including contributor reporting, disbursements, amendments, waivers and other BF-specific requirements. Monitor risks relevant to donor-funded guarantees or other BF instruments in coordination with IFC portfolio teams. Capture lessons from executed investments and feed these into subsequent structuring, pipeline selection and facility design. Support preparation of transaction case studies and impact examples for contributors and internal stakeholders. Selection Criteria MBA or Master's degree, preferably with specialization in finance, economics or a related discipline. At least 8 years of experience, although preference will be given to candidate with at least 15 years of relevant investment experience, preferably involving cross-border emerging-market transactions and complex real-sector investments. Strong demonstrated experience in structuring and executing debt, guarantees, structured finance, equity/quasi-equity or other risk-sharing instruments. Strong understanding of project finance and financial modelling, including the ability to distinguish between project viability constraints and financing-market constraints requiring BF intervention. Direct experience with blended or concessional finance and familiarity with the DFI Enhanced Blended Concessional Finance Principles. Good understanding of IFC's investment cycle, credit processes, BFC governance and portfolio-management requirements. Experience working with DFIs, MDBs, bilateral development institutions and/or donor-funded facilities. Familiarity with European development-finance institutions and the European Commission/EFSD+ architecture would be strongly preferred. Strong commercial judgment and ability to evaluate whether BF is necessary, what risk BF should address, and what represents minimum concessionality. Ability to proactively originate opportunities and work effectively with investment teams rather than operate primarily as a facility administrator. Strong analytical skills and ability to synthesize market and competitor intelligence into actionable implications for IFC. Excellent stakeholder-management and communication skills. Excellent written and spoken English. French would be a significant advantage; other European languages would be beneficial. Ability to use commercially available LLM tools like Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot for research, analysis, and drafting in investments, validate outputs against primary sources, and remain accountable for recommendations WBG Culture Attributes Sense of urgency: Anticipate and quickly respond to the needs of internal and external stakeholders. Thoughtful risk-taking: Challenge the status quo and push boundaries to achieve greater impact. Empowerment and accountability: Empower yourself and others to act and hold each other accountable for results.
